He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech Red Raiders]], [[Florida Atlantic Owls men's basketball|Florida Atlantic Owls]] and [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. Goldin earned all-conference honors three times in his college career, including a first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] selection in 2025. ==Early life and high school career== Goldin was born in [[Nalchik]], Russia{{cite web|url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2023/01/13/dusty-may-has-fau-basketball-on-cusp-of-first-ever-top-25-ranking/69804275007/|title=Dusty May has FAU basketball on cusp of first-ever Top 25 ranking|work=[[The Palm Beach Post]]|date=13 January 2023|archive-date=15 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230115230932/https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2023/01/13/dusty-may-has-fau-basketball-on-cusp-of-first-ever-top-25-ranking/69804275007/?utm_campaign=snd-autopilot&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter_pbpost|access-date=27 March 2023}} and later moved with his family to [[Voronezh]], where he grew up.{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/i_0y3fM3N74?si=yVH3bWzf1g3xPhJG&t=3165/|title=ВЛАД ГОЛДИН Взял Мяч Майами Хит, драфт НБА, контракты, Мозгов и Воронеж – большое интервью|date=12 July 2025|access-date=15 July 2025}} He was a competitive wrestler until age 15 and then began playing basketball after a significant growth spurt.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4350038/2023/03/27/fau-vladislav-goldin-russia-final-four/|title=FAU center Vladislav Goldin grew up wrestling in Russia. Now he’s in the Final Four|first=Rustin|last=Dodd|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=27 March 2023|access-date=27 March 2023}} Goldin played for [[PBC CSKA Junior]] for three seasons.{{cite March 2023}} ==College career== ===Texas Tech=== Goldin began his college career at Texas Tech. He played in ten games during his freshman season and averaged 1.9 points and one rebound per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/owls/2023/03/25/vladislav-goldin-fau-basketball-center-florida-atlantic/70048868007/|title=Vlad Goldin: 3 things to know about FAU basketball big man|work=[[The Palm Beach Post]]|date=25 March 2023|archive-date=26 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230326004516/https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/owls/2023/03/25/vladislav-goldin-fau-basketball-center-florida-atlantic/70048868007/|access-date=27 March 2023}} Following the end of the season, Goldin entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]].{{cite web|url=https://www.lubbockonline.com/story/sports/college/2021/04/12/jamarius-burton-latest-texas-tech-player-testing-waters-via-transfer-portal/7192995002/|title=Jamarius Burton latest Texas Tech player testing waters via transfer portal|work=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]]|date=12 April 2021|access-date=27 March 2023}} ===Florida Atlantic=== Goldin transferred to [[Florida Atlantic University]] (FAU) in 2021.{{cite web|url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/owls/2021/04/16/bitumba-baruti-vladislav-goldin-transferring-fau-mens-basketball-owls-dusty-may/7253737002/|title=Bitumba Baruti, Vladislav Goldin transferring to FAU men's basketball|work=[[The Palm Beach Post]]|date=16 April 2021|archive-date=16 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210416155633/https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/owls/2021/04/16/bitumba-baruti-vladislav-goldin-transferring-fau-mens-basketball-owls-dusty-may/7253737002/|access-date=27 March 2023}} He averaged 6.8 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.1 blocks per game in his first season with the [[Florida Atlantic Owls men's basketball|Owls]].{{cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/vladislav-goldin-fau-florida-atlantic-number-50/hxr8pehl5b3eozoudada0pxi|title=Who is FAU's number 50? Everything to know about Russian big man Vladislav Goldin|first=Sam|last=Jarden|work=[[Sporting News]]|date=25 March 2023|access-date=27 March 2023}} In his second season with the Owls, Goldin was named third-team All-[[Conference USA]], averaging 10.2 points per game, 6.5 rebounds and 1.2 blocked shots.{{cite web|url=https://www.wpbf.com/article/fau-rakes-in-conference-awards-hope-to-win-league-tournament-next/43239667|title=FAU rakes in conference awards; hope to win league tournament next|first=Yianni|last=Kourakis|website=[[WPBF]].com|date=7 March 2023|access-date=27 March 2023}} He scored 14 points and 13 rebounds in FAU's 79–76 win over Kansas State in the Elite Eight of the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2023 NCAA tournament]], leading the owls to the [[NCAA]] [[Final Four]].{{cite web|url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/ncaa/article273605410.html|title=K-State Wildcats vs. FAU Owls: Vlad Goldin handshake snub|work=[[Miami Herald]]|date=26 March 2023|access-date=27 March 2023}} In his third season with the Owls, fourth total, Goldin averaged 15.7 points per game, 6.9 rebounds and 1.6 blocked shots, leading FAU back to the NCAA tournament. After the season, he was named second-team All-[[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) following the Owls change in conference.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/vladislav-goldin-1.html|title=Vladislav Goldin Statistics|website=Sports Reference - CBB}} ===Michigan=== On April 29, 2024, Goldin withdrew from the [[NBA draft]] process. Instead, he transferred to the [[University of Michigan]] to join his former FAU head coach, [[Dusty May]], in [[Ann Arbor]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2024/04/29/vladislav-goldin-transfer-michigan-basketball-dusty-may/73498253007/|title=FAU center Vladislav Goldin reuniting with Dusty May on Michigan basketball|website=Detroit Free Press}} Goldin and current Michigan guard [[Nimari Burnett]] were both teammates and roommates as members of [[2020–21 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team#Recruits|Texas Tech’s 2020 recruiting class]].{{cite web|url=https://texastech.com/news/2020/7/9/mens-basketball-vladislav-goldin-signs-with-texas-tech|title=Vladislav Goldin Signs With Texas Tech|accessdate=April 29, 2024|date=July 9, 2020|website=Texastech.com}} Goldin earned the starting center position for the Michigan Wolverines. On December 3, 2024, against [[2024–25 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]], Goldin had 24 points, adding five rebounds and three blocked shots.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2024/12/03/michigan-basketball-stuns-wisconsin-67-64-despite-frigid-1st-half/76752779007/|title= 7-footers lift Michigan basketball after brutal start to 67-64 upset of No. 11 Wisconsin|work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=December 3, 2024 |access-date=December 3, 2024}} On December 7 against [[2024–25 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Iowa]], he scored a game-high 20 points and 11 rebounds for his first double-double of the season.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2024/12/7/mens-basketball-michigan-holds-off-iowa-to-close-early-big-ten-slate |title=Michigan Holds Off Iowa to Close Early Big Ten Slate |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |website=MGoBlue.com |date=December 7, 2024 |access-date=December 7, 2024}} During that week, he averaged 22.0 points, 8.0 rebounds, 2.0 blocks and shot 62.5 percent (15-for-24) from the field. He was subsequently named the [[Big Ten]] Player of the Week on December 9.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2024/12/9/2024-25-michigan-mens-basketball-awards-and-honors |title=Awards and Honors: Goldin Earns B1G Player of the Week |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |website=MGoBlue.com |date=December 9, 2024 |access-date=December 9, 2024}} On December 18 against [[2024–25 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team|Oklahoma]], Goldin scored a then career-high 26 points, 11 rebounds and three blocked shots.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2024/12/18/michigan-basketball-score-vs-oklahoma-jumpman-invitational-87-86/77078007007/|title=Michigan basketball loses 87-86 to Oklahoma on crushing 4-point play in Jumpman Invitational |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |first=Tony |last=Garcia |date=December 18, 2024 |access-date=December 18, 2024}} On January 7, 2025 against [[2024–25 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]], Goldin scored a career-high 36 points with seven rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2025/01/08/michigans-vladislav-goldin-scores-career-high-36-in-94-75-win-at-ucla/77528154007/|title=Michigan's Vladislav Goldin scores career-high 36 points in 94-75 victory at UCLA|work=Detroit Free Press}} Against the four ranked teams Michigan played to date, Goldin averaged 26.0 points, 7.0 rebounds, 2.25 blocks and shot 70.9 percent from the floor. In doing so, he became the first NCAA division 1 player in the last 25 years to average over 25.0 points and shoot at least 70 percent from the field in a four-game span against ranked opponents.{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/michigan/basketball/michigan-wolverines-vlad-goldin-achieves-feat-not-seen-in-mens-college-basketball-for-25-years-vs-ap-poll-top-25-opponents|title=Michigan's Vlad Goldin achieves feat not seen in men's college basketball for 25 years|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} The 36 points were the most by a Wolverine since [[Daniel Horton (basketball)|Daniel Horton]] posted 39 on February 21, 2006 for the [[2005–06 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2005–06 Wolverines]]. For the week, he averaged 27.5 points, 7.0 rebounds, and 2.5 assists while shooting 76%, to earn Co-Big Ten Player of the Week on January 13.{{cite web|url=https://bigten.org/mbb/article/bltd68729cc7de90b47/|title=Iowa, Michigan, USC Score Men’s Basketball Weekly Accolades|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=January 13, 2025|access-date=January 13, 2025}} On January 19 against [[2024–25 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|Northwestern]], Goldin had 31 points, eight rebounds and four blocks; his second career game scoring over 30 points.{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2025/01/michigan-beats-northwestern-in-overtime-behind-vladislav-goldins-huge-game.html?outputType=amp|title=Michigan beats Northwestern in overtime behind Vladislav Goldin’s huge game|website=MLive}} On March 5 against [[2024–25 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Maryland]], he had 20 points and a career-high 15 rebounds, his fifth double-double of the season.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/3/5/mens-basketball-u-m-late-game-rally-stifled-in-setback-to-no-13-maryland-in-home-finals |title=U-M Late-Game Rally Stifled in Setback to No. 13 Maryland in Home Finale |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |date=March 5, 2025 |access-date=March 5, 2025}} In March, Goldin was named a finalist for the [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar Award]], given to the nation’s best [[Center (basketball)|center]] each season.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2025/03/07/michigan-basketball-vladislav-goldin-finalist-kareem-abdul-jabbar-award/81971648007/ |title=Vlad Goldin finalist for Kareem Abdul-Jabbar Award as nation's best C |website=[[Detroit Free Press]]|author=Tony Garcia|date=March 7, 2025}} He also earned first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] honors, selected by the media.{{cite web|url=https://umhoops.com/2025/03/11/vlad-goldin-earns-first-team-all-big-ten-honors-wolf-named-to-second-team/ |title=Goldin earns First Team All-Big Ten honors, Wolf named to Second Team |website=UM Hoops |author=Dylan Burkhardt |date=March 11, 2025 |access-date=March 11, 2025}} Along with being awarded the [[Most valuable player|MVP]] of the [[2025 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|2025 Big Ten tournament]] after leading Michigan to a Big Ten championship.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/3/16/mens-basketball-michigan-wins-2025-big-ten-tournament-championship-over-wisconsin |title=U-M Downs No. 18 Wisconsin to Capture B1G Tournament Title Wisconsin 59-53 for Big Ten title |website=CBS News |date=March 16, 2025 |access-date=March 16, 2025}} On March 22, in the Second Round of the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2025 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=March 22, 2025 |access-date=March 22, 2025}} ==Professional career== On June 26, Goldin signed a two-way contract with the [[Miami Heat]] after going unselected in the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.on3.com/pro/news/miami-heat-sign-vlad-goldin-contract-2025-nba-draft-michigan-undrafted-free-agent/ |title=Miami Heat sign Vlad Goldin to contract after minutes, including an 18-point, 10-rebound, 4-block finale in which he scored the game-winner with 11 seconds left in a 93–92 victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/michigan/football/son-of-michigan-coach-stays-home-wolverines-begin-building-their-2027-class-|title=Former Michigan big Vlad Goldin hits game-winner for Miami Skyforce]], Goldin was called up to the Heat roster in response to an injury to [[Bam Adebayo]].{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/heat/onsi/news/heat-call-up-two-way-center-vladislav-goldin-with-bam-adebayo-out-vs-hornets-01k9e76kdyq2|title=Heat call up two-way center Vladislav Goldin with Bam Adebayo out vs. Hornets|accessdate=November 15, 2025|date=November 7, 2025|publisher=[[NBA.com]]}} In his G League debut on November 21, against the [[Wisconsin Herd]], he posted 23 points and 9 rebounds, making 10 of 13 [[field goal (basketball)|field goal]] attempts including both of his [[three point shot]] attempts.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/game/sxf-vs-wis-2052500084?view=game-story|title=SIOUX FALLS COMMANDS 135-121 VICTORY OVER WISCONSIN|accessdate=November 24, 2025|date=November 21, 2025|publisher=[[NBA.com]]}} With seven Heat players sidelined, he made his NBA debut on December 19, 2025 in the final minute of play against the [[2025-26 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article313040126.html|title=Heat, missing seven players, loses in Boston. Takeaways and details|accessdate=December 20, 2025|date=December 19, 2025|work=[[Miami Herald]]|author=Jackson Barry}} He played the final 55 seconds and tallied one assist.{{cite web|url=https://news.sportbox.ru/Vidy_sporta/Basketbol/NBA/spbnews_NI2279671_Vladislav_Goldin_provel_debutnyj_match_v_NBA|title=Vladislav Goldin played his debut match in the NBA|accessdate=December 20, 2025|date=December 20, 2025|website=Sportbox.ru|publisher=National Sports TV Channel}} On February 1, Goldin scored his first NBA points on a [[Jumpman (logo)|Jumpman]] style [[slam dunk]] during a three game in four night set against the [[2025-26 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401810560|title=Heat build 54-point lead, roll past Bulls 134-91 with Adebayo, Larsson each scoring 20|accessdate=February 2, 2026|date=February 1, 2026|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} The Heat extended a two-way contract for the 2026 season on June 29, 2026.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-extend-two-way-qualifying-offer-to-goldin|title=HEAT EXTEND TWO-WAY QUALIFYING OFFER TO GOLDIN|accessdate=July 1, 2026|date=June 29, 2026|publisher=[[NBA.com]]}} Goldin was announced on June 30, 2026 as a member of the [[2026 NBA Summer League]] roster for the Miami Heat.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-announce-summer-league-information-2026|title=HEAT Announce Summer League Information|accessdate=July 1, 2026|date=June 30, 2026|publisher=[[NBA.com]]}}
